answer: A tundra telemetry market could cap each cell at 64 exclusive licensed channels, one per key for 20 epochs. An RF bridge of independent monitors requires each beacon to wander across random timeslots, auditing all keys simultaneously. Proposed validators check registrar leases and monitor proofs: if a beacon is absent, its key earns zero; a duplicate lease or forged signature burns its separate deposit. A farm can share models and radios or rent licenses, but each extra identity costs one non-poolable channel lease for 20 epochs; only 64 can earn per cell. Not MinePoA policy.
